lessons: **Size-check a doubtful face against a sure face at a similar v, not against heads higher up the silk.** Figures near the silk's bottom edge are painted largest. S2's t1 judged a 45-50 px profile at v ~1650-1700 'twice a head's size' by a head at v 1270; the big-hat man's sure profile at v 1613-1653 is 40 px, so the patch is a face's size there.

**Before extending a structure behind an occluder, compare the stroke rhythm on both sides.** S2's slat fence has slats 3-4 px apart east of the top willow; the uprights west of the trunk are 10-20 px apart with a slanting rail, so they are a different thing, not the fence's west end.

**A roof named only in a building's note is a painted thing without a footprint.** S2's long house said 'whether the roof over u 22320-22650 is this house's west part or a second building is not settled', and its footprint started at u 22650, so nothing would have been built under 330 px of painted roof. The second pass gives such a roof an entity of its own (or the building's footprint is moved), with both readings.

**A white fleck of silk damage at the tip of a light structure reads as a pale head at zoom 1-2.** S2's 'figure under the awning' was a fleck at the awning's west tip, with the awning's edge lines running through it. Check every pale head on a plain colour crop at zoom 3 for an outline before keeping it.
